=== 1. THE RATIO BETWEEN FITTINGS AND FILL — THE HEADLINE ===

Across six public/social spaces the fill sits at 4-10% of the key. It is astonishingly consistent, and the one space that breaks it breaks it for a reason.

The cleanest instance is Casino.webp, because it is ONE surface, ONE material, ONE depth, alternately lit and shadowed by a grille: the deck at (0.28,0.90)-(0.40,1.00) carries hard diagonal stripes; balanced, the lit stripes peak at Y 0.50-0.63 (p97 0.583) and the troughs between them sit at Y 0.11-0.18, with the deepest ground at Y 0.043. Trough/peak = 0.073 to 0.23. That is a direct photometric statement: block the room's key and 7-23% of the illumination remains.

The second cleanest is conference aerea.webp, a near-plan view where a horizontal profile across the floor at y 0.62-0.66 reads: 0.05-0.08 outside the pool, a rise from 0.08 to 0.78 across Δx 0.06 of frame width, a flat 0.44-0.78 across the medallion, and a fall back to 0.05. Off-pool/pool = 0.083. The rise and fall are SHARP — that pool has an edge, so the fitting is a spot with a defined cone, not an omni.

Per space (darkest measurable surface / brightest lit surface, balanced):
  fresh_air_restaurant   0.041   dougs_dugout   0.09    zocalo_concourse  0.094
  conference_lounge      0.100   casino         0.074   council_chamber   0.21

Whole-frame check, balanced luminance with clipped sources excluded, p50/p95:
  Doug's Dugout 0.060 (56.2% of the frame below Y 0.05) · Fresh Air 0.118 (54.5%) ·
  more zocalo 0.138 (35.1%) · conference aerea 0.167 · zocalo 0.241 · Casino 0.345 ·
  council chambers 0.397 (only 8.4%) · Earhart's 0.523.

So: SET AMBIENT/GI AT ROUGHLY 0.08 OF THE KEY IN A SOCIAL SPACE, AND AT 0.20 IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER. The ceremonial room is the only one in the family that is lit like a room rather than like a set of pools, and that difference is the sector's identity, not an accident of exposure.

WHAT LOOKS LIKE AMBIENT IS NOT AMBIENT — IT IS COLOURED SPILL. In conference aerea the floor away from the medallion reads H 190-200 S 0.63-0.86 on the left (the cyan floor track) and H 21-44 S 0.18-0.47 on the right (the warm table lamps). One continuous floor, two hues 170 degrees apart. Same test on one table: its left side reads normalised (0.742, 0.873, 1.000) and its right side (1.000, 0.807, 0.809). That is NEGATIVE_RESULTS' signature for the sixth and seventh time, and here it is the answer rather than the warning: a B5 social interior has NO neutral fill term. Every photon on a dark surface came from a named fitting. A grey ambient will kill these rooms.

A SECOND, DIFFERENT RATIO — AND DO NOT CONFUSE THEM. On the Zocalo deck a chair leg casts shadows only 0.74 as dark as the deck beside them (profile at y 0.965-0.975: lit 0.63-0.70, trough 0.47-0.55), and ONE leg casts two to three distinct shadows at once (magnified crop of more zocalo.png at (0.05,0.78)-(0.40,1.00)). That is not fill — it is overlap. At zocalo.py's 2.7 m pool pitch under a 7.2 m ceiling the spacing/height ratio is 0.375, so the pools merge completely and the deck shows no periodicity at all (constant-depth scan x 0.17-0.42 runs 0.57-0.68 with no dips). Blocking one of ~4 contributors leaves 74%. So: DEEP shadow where a fitting is the only source (Fresh Air, under a table: 0.017 against a lit deck of 0.414, i.e. 0.04); SHALLOW shadow on the concourse deck where four fittings overlap.

AND THE THING THE ZOCALO ACTUALLY IS: a bright floor under a black ceiling. Balanced, the deck under the downlights reads Y 0.657 while the soffit above reads 0.062, the purlin run 0.062 and the gallery slab edge 0.028. Ratio 0.04-0.09. The arch scanlines reproduce materials.py's claim — row peaks 0.485/0.619/0.647/0.851 against row medians 0.102/0.127/0.130/0.093, ratio 0.10-0.21.

=== 2. WHERE THE FITTINGS ARE ===

Placement in interior_kit.py and zocalo.py is already sourced and I did not re-derive it; I reproduce it in the fixtures list in metres and add what the frames measure:

 · Zocalo deck pools: x ±4.7 m, z 1.35/4.05/6.75/9.45 per 10.8 m bay (2.7 m pitch), pool 1.57 m, ceiling 7.2 m. spacing/height 0.375 → merged wash, no visible pooling. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ENGINE: kit.downlight_pool() models the POOL, not the lens. In more zocalo.png the deck carries cast shadows from chairs and feet, so its brightness is from OVERHEAD sources; the disc must be a SpotLight above deck aimed down (cone half-angle ≥ 50° to merge at that pitch) with the disc as its baked core, not an emissive floor plate.
 · Zocalo rib lamps: 5 per rib at (x, y) = (±5.52, 3.27), (±3.38, 5.72), (0.00, 6.78) m; ribs every 5.4 m; 10 per bay.
 · Zocalo stall festoon: awning eave at 2.29 m. zocalo.py places 6-9 bulbs per stall. MEASURED, zocalo.webp (0.00,0.14)-(0.32,0.30): 64 discrete bulb blobs, median area 8 px, median nearest-neighbour spacing 7.8 px = 2.6 bulb-diameters. Scaled on the 3.0 m awning (≈95 px/m) that is a pitch of ~0.08 m and 60-100 bulbs per stall, swagged over the whole canopy frame. The module is out by roughly a factor of ten, and it matters for energy: 64 tiny bulbs and 7 bright ones are different objects.
 · Fresh Air overhead run: warm rectangular downlights mounted ON the red structural tubes, detected by blob analysis at frame (0.192,0.210) (0.367,0.318) (0.441,0.108) (0.482,0.390) (0.584,0.257) (0.671,0.349) (0.877,0.174) (0.911,0.296). Grouped by tube slope they sit at 0.33-0.44 of frame width apart while each fitting is 0.026-0.047 wide — a pitch of 9-13 fitting-lengths. At a 0.6 m fitting that is 5.5-7.5 m, which brackets zocalo.py's 5.4 m rib pitch from an unrelated room.
 · Casino: two large gridded backlit panels HIGH on the wall (frame (0.037,0.049)-(0.138,0.262) and (0.694,0.139)-(0.817,0.287)), a ring of ~24 filament bulbs at 1-2.5 m, a continuous mint bar-back strip at counter height, a cyan tube along the balustrade at ~1.0 m.
 · conference aerea: overhead spot on the floor medallion (fitting out of frame); a lit panel ON each table top at ~0.75 m; a cyan tube inlaid in the step nosing AT DECK LEVEL running a hexagon round the dais; arcs of cool louvred slits at high level.
 · Doug's Dugout: pendants below standing eye height, one per table, as hospitality.py records.

=== 3. COLOUR TEMPERATURE, AND THE ONE CORRECTION THAT MATTERS ===

THERE ARE TWO WARM REGISTERS AND THE LIBRARY ONLY HAS ONE. Every architectural fitting that actually lights a public room measures 4000-5000 K:
  Fresh Air tube downlights   (1.000, 0.86, 0.72) sRGB  ~4200-4500 K  (dE to the Planckian locus 0.006-0.019 — these are near-perfect blackbodies)
  Casino backlit wall panels  (1.000, 0.96, 0.87)       ~5200-5700 K
  conference aerea pool+lamps (1.000, 0.79, 0.70)       ~4000 K
  Doug's Dugout pendant       (1.000, 0.77, 0.66)       ~3900 K
while the small decorative practicals measure 2000-3000 K:
  Casino bulb wheel (1.000, 0.548, 0.393) ~2220 K (hue rock-steady H 13-15 across a 4.4x value ladder — a real tint, not a cast)
  Zocalo rib lamp   (1.000, 0.664, 0.520) ~2990 K
  Zocalo wordmark   (1.000, 0.520, 0.300) ~2000 K

materials.light_downlight ships emission (1.0, 0.68, 0.40) = ~2790 K, and ACCENTS['warm_practical'] ships (1.000, 0.612, 0.353) = ~2440 K. THE SHIPPED VALUE CONTRADICTS ITS OWN CITATION: light_downlight's source line records grey level 1.webp's lens at balanced H 27 S 0.238, and H 27 / S 0.238 / V 1.0 is (1.000, 0.869, 0.762) — 4600 K, which is my family's architectural register to within 0.01 in every channel. ACCENTS' own note says it took "Casino H21 S0.457 lifted to source level", and lifting is backwards: a neutral surface under a single source takes the source's hue exactly, so a lit surface bounds the source's saturation from ABOVE, not below. If layer 4 hangs (1.0, 0.68, 0.40) on every light_downlight in the station, every pale wall goes sodium-orange. The deep-amber value is correct for the bulb-wheel/festoon/neon class and wrong for the downlight class.

THE SPACES MIX REGISTERS, AND THE MIX IS THE LOOK. Every one of the six is a warm key against a cyan or cool-blue fill:
  Zocalo   — WARM overhead (rib lamps 2990 K, festoon, neon) against a COOL deck. The lit deck balances normalised (0.851, 0.992, 1.000) on the left and (0.581, 0.789, 1.000) under the blue practical on the right; one continuous deck, H 173-183 vs H 203-210.
  conference aerea — WARM 4000 K key against a CYAN floor track (0.362, 0.901, 1.000) and a COOL-BLUE louvre perimeter (0.690, 0.809, 1.000), plus a genuinely MAGENTA backlit chequer panel at H 299-302, constant across a 1.7x value range.
  Casino   — 5200-5700 K panels against a MINT bar-back (0.725, 1.000, 0.965), a cyan rail (0.716, 0.934, 1.000) and cool-blue table felt.
  Fresh Air— 4400 K tube downlights + one 6500 K neutral batten against CYAN neon (0.476, 0.978, 1.000, which reproduces ACCENTS['cyan_neon']) and a large cyan backlit garden wall.
  Council  — the outlier again: its brightest surface, the perforated table fascia, balances to S 0.021, i.e. NEUTRAL. The chamber is one even neutral wash with a cool-blue wall accent. No warm register at all.
So SECTOR_ACCENT's "red → warm_practical, green → cyan_neon" is advisory and half right: both sectors carry both, and it is the SPLIT between key and fill that identifies them, not a single hue.

EARHART'S IS THE EMISSIVE-WINDOW DATUM, and it is directly relevant to the standing blocking finding against exterior_approach. Raw, the glazed band's interior clusters run H 216-265 across a 20x value range — a genuine cool-blue, ~9900 K, brightest resolved cluster (0.787, 0.872, 1.000). The lit band peaks at Y 0.613 against the daylit hull shell above it at Y 0.350, i.e. a lit window band reads ~1.75x the surface beside it, and the dark interior voids between bays read Y 0.031, i.e. 0.09x that shell. So an emissive window band is NOT a uniform glow: it is a 1.75x/0.09x checker, and the dark bays are what makes it read as a building.

=== 4. SHADOWS — WHICH ONES EARN THEIR FRAME TIME ===

CAST BY SOMETHING, ALWAYS. Casino.webp is the proof that these rooms have a directional key: the grille shadow on the deck is hard-edged (0.13 to 0.55 across ~7-11 px of an 814-wide frame), repeating and crisp along its whole run, thrown from the upper left, i.e. by the left backlit panel. The Casino's mural, by contrast, is washed almost evenly by those same panels: across x 0.14-0.66 at y 0.10-0.20 it runs Y 0.386-0.539, min/max 0.72, and between the two panels it is still 0.83-0.89 of the value under one. THE RULE THE FAMILY GIVES: AREA PANELS WASH (0.8 across a bay), POINT PRACTICALS POOL (0.08). Both exist; do not model one with the other.

Worth shadows: the Casino wall panels (the only hard shadow in the family and a signature of the room); the Fresh Air tube downlights (the under-table shadow at 0.04 of the lit deck is the deepest reading in the family and is what makes that room read); the conference-lounge medallion spot (a hard-edged pool that a standing figure must break); one Zocalo deck downlight per bay; the two or three nearest Dugout pendants.
Not worth shadows: the Zocalo rib lamps (10 per bay, set into the arch they light, nothing occludes them), the stall festoon (60-100 bulbs, each negligible), the neon, the shopfront screens, the deck strip, the conference-lounge floor track (it is the FILL — shadowing an uplight both costs and lies), the conference table lamps, the council chamber's louvres.
And the cheap win the Zocalo measurement licenses: because ~4 deck downlights overlap at any point and the measured shadow depth is 0.74, turning shadows off on three of every four costs about 25% of one fitting's contribution. That is a real, measured budget for a real, measured error.

=== CAVEATS, STATED PLAINLY ===
 · Doug's Dugout was measured RAW ONLY and only for emitters, per NEGATIVE_RESULTS. Its pendant colour is read off the brightest resolved lit object under the pool (the bun, raw (0.867, 0.663, 0.569), normalised (1.000, 0.765, 0.656)); the deep H 0-8 readings everywhere else in that frame are the objects' own colour plus falloff, not the lamp.
 · Grey-world is circular for a single-illuminant frame: it removes the average cast, which in a one-key room is the key. It is trustworthy HERE because these rooms are two-register — the residual after balancing splits warm one way and cyan the other, which is the signal. Where I balanced a source rather than a lit surface (conference aerea's table lamps) I say so and cross-check against the surface it lights.
 · conference aerea's medallion floor is assumed neutral-albedo. If it is a warm terrazzo, its 4000 K reads too warm. One frame of that floor under a different light would close it.
 · The Fresh Air fitting pitch of 5.5-7.5 m rests on an assumed 0.6 m fitting length; the ratio (9-13 fitting-lengths) is the measurement and survives whatever the length is.

fixtures.reasoning: This is the AREA source of the family and it behaves completely differently from the point practicals: the mural it washes runs balanced Y 0.386-0.539 across x 0.14-0.66 (min/max 0.72) and is still at 0.83-0.89 midway between the two panels. Area panels wash; point practicals pool. It is also the only fitting in the whole family that throws a hard-edged shadow, so it earns its shadow map.

fixtures.placement: ring of ~24 individual filament bulbs round a 1.6 m wheel-of-fortune, hub at roughly 1.6 m, bulbs from 1.0 to 2.5 m

This is the reading materials.ACCENTS records as 'Casino H21 S0.457' and is the true home of the deep-amber register.
fixtures.extrapolated: energy_rel 0.20 and range 3.0 m. Twenty-four small bulbs on a signage wheel do not light a casino; the frame shows their reach falling off within a couple of metres of the wheel, but no surface at a known distance resolves cleanly enough to put a number on it.
fixtures.reasoning: 2220 K, and it is a decorative fitting, not an architectural one. This is the register ACCENTS['warm_practical'] was derived from, and it is correct HERE and wrong for downlights -- which is the single most consequential thing in this report.

fixtures.placement: continuous horizontal strip along the bar back, roughly 1.1-1.4 m above deck, ~10 m run

fixtures.extrapolated: energy_rel and range. The strip is a wide backlit band behind a crowd, so nothing clean stands next to it at a known distance; 0.3 is set from its share of the frame's mid-tones and its visible reach onto the mural above it, where the balanced hue swings to H 154-180 across the whole middle of the wall.
fixtures.reasoning: It is the reason the Casino's mural balances H 154-180 across its whole middle while reading H 51 at the left edge next to the warm panel: one wall, two lights, 120 degrees apart. Include it or the room's cool half disappears.

fixtures.placement: cyan tube run along the top of the balustrade rail, ~1.0 m above deck
fixtures.extrapolated: energy_rel and range, both set from its visible reach along the rail and onto the deck immediately below it.
fixtures.reasoning: A rail-height cyan line. Same family as the conference lounge's floor track: B5 puts its cool register LOW and its warm register HIGH, over and over.

fixtures.placement: small rectangular fitting clamped to the red structural tubes crossing the volume overhead, aimed down; pitch 9-13 fitting-lengths along each tube, several parallel tube runs
fixtures.source: reference/04-sector-red/Fresh air.webp (authority 1). NEW GAINS, computed here: (1.0027, 0.9306, 1.0774), n=562,113. Blob analysis (luminance > 0.30, R > B + 0.02) locates the fittings at frame (0.192,0.210) (0.367,0.318) (0.441,0.108) (0.482,0.390) (0.584,0.257) (0.671,0.349) (0.877,0.174) (0.911,0.296), 22-47 px wide, Lmax 0.82-1.00. COLOUR from the resolved (unclipped) medians: C (0.416,0.357,0.294) H 31, D (0.582,0.496,0.392) H 33, B (0.588,0.547,0.463) H 40, normalising to (1.000, 0.858, 0.707), (1.000, 0.852, 0.674) and (1.000, 0.930, 0.787). Mean (1.000, 0.860, 0.715) sRGB, linear (1.000, 0.711, 0.470); CCT 4240-4990 K with dE to the Planckian locus of 0.006-0.019 -- these are near-perfect blackbodies. SPACING: grouped by tube slope the fittings sit 0.33-0.44 of frame width apart against a fitting width of 0.026-0.047, i.e. 9-13 fitting-lengths. SHADOW: the deck under a table edge at (0.415,0.930)-(0.470,0.960) reads balanced Y 0.017 against the open deck at (0.31,0.955)-(0.47,0.995) at Y 0.414 -- a ratio of 0.041, the deepest occlusion shadow in the family.
fixtures.extrapolated: spacing_m 6.0 assumes a 0.6 m fitting; the RATIO, 9-13 fitting-lengths, is the measurement and survives any assumption about the length. range_m 16 is set by the height of the tube runs above the tables, judged from the canopy, not measured.
fixtures.reasoning: The best-behaved measurement in the family: three independent fittings in one frame, all resolved, all landing within 0.08 of each other and all within 0.02 of the Planckian locus. 4400 K, NOT 2790 K. This is the number light_downlight should be carrying, and its own citation (grey level 1.webp, balanced H 27 S 0.238 = (1.000, 0.869, 0.762)) agrees with me and not with its shipped value.

fixtures.placement: one large neutral-white batten hung well below the tube runs, roughly 4-5 m above the tables, over the entrance side

fixtures.reasoning: A genuinely neutral 6500 K fitting sitting in the same room as 4400 K downlights and cyan neon. Worth carrying because a room whose every light is warm has no white in it, and this is the frame's white.

fixtures.placement: curved cyan tubes tracing the restaurant fascia above the sign, and a second run lower at roughly 3 m

fixtures.placement: large raked backlit panel behind the planting at low level, roughly 0.5-3 m above deck, spanning half the room's width
fixtures.extrapolated: energy_rel 0.4, from its size and its visible reach into the planting in front of it; no surface at a known distance resolves against it.
fixtures.reasoning: The room's whole cool half, at LOW level again, under warm fittings at high level. That vertical split -- warm above, cool below -- recurs in four of the six spaces and is the most transferable compositional rule in this family.

fixtures.placement: slim vertical tube fittings standing among the planting between the tables, roughly 1.2-2.0 m tall
fixtures.extrapolated: energy_rel, range and the 3.0 m spacing, which is read off how many appear across the visible planting rather than measured against anything.
fixtures.reasoning: A third cool register in one room. These are the fittings that separate figures from the dark planting behind them at eye level -- without them the crowd merges into the foliage, which is exactly what a naive engine build will produce.

fixtures.placement: single broad overhead spot on axis above the raised floor medallion, fitting out of frame; the pool is coincident with the medallion and has a HARD edge
fixtures.source: reference/05-sector-green/conference aerea.webp (authority 1), gains recomputed as 1.1216/1.0263/0.8818, reproducing GREY_WORLD_GAINS. Balanced, the medallion's pale annulus reads 0.550/0.612/0.512 (Y 0.591) at (0.400,0.583)-(0.450,0.667) and 0.702/0.555/0.467 H 23 S 0.335 (Y 0.580) at (0.620,0.600)-(0.690,0.680). Normalised (1.000, 0.791, 0.665) sRGB, linear (1.000, 0.589, 0.400), ~3950 K. THE EDGE IS MEASURED: a horizontal profile at y 0.62-0.66 reads 0.05-0.08 outside, rises 0.08 -> 0.78 across dx 0.06 of frame width, holds 0.44-0.78 across the disc, and falls back to 0.05 by x 0.78. The vertical profile does the same at y 0.77-0.80.

The colour assumes the medallion terrazzo is neutral -- if it is warm, this reads too warm, and one frame of that floor under a different light closes it.
fixtures.reasoning: The single best demonstration in the family that these are SPOTS, not omnis: an omni cannot produce a rise from 0.08 to 0.78 across 6% of a frame. Off-pool floor at 0.083 of pool. A figure standing in it must occlude it, so it casts.

fixtures.placement: a lit panel set into each table top, ~0.75 m above deck, one per table, 5-6 visible in the room

The honest reading is on the LIT SURFACES beside the lamps, balanced: table tops at (0.265,0.510)-(0.300,0.545) normalise (1.000, 0.807, 0.809), at (0.800,0.545)-(0.830,0.585) (1.000, 0.878, 0.786), at (0.660,0.815)-(0.700,0.855) (1.000, 0.671, 0.577). fixtures.reasoning: THE TWO-LIGHT TEST, run on one table: its lamp side normalises (1.000, 0.807, 0.809) and its far side, facing the cyan floor track, normalises (0.742, 0.873, 1.000). One table, two sides, two illuminants, ~170 degrees apart. That is the whole design of this room in one object.

fixtures.placement: cyan tube inlaid in the step nosing AT DECK LEVEL, running a hexagon around the raised dais; the room's only floor-level fitting

ITS REACH IS MEASURED: the floor at (0.170,0.640)-(0.240,0.700) reads balanced H 197 S 0.807, at (0.05,0.75)-(0.15,0.85) H 200 S 0.725, and the step riser at (0.30,0.34)-(0.40,0.40) H 195 S 0.589 -- everything within a few metres of the track carries its hue at very high saturation.

Do not shadow it -- it is an uplight and shadowing an uplight both costs frame time and under-lights the very surfaces it exists to reach.

fixtures.placement: arcs of narrow vertical louvred slits round the upper perimeter of the rotunda, high level, above head height

The right-hand arc at (0.70,0.11)-(0.88,0.18) gives H 216 independently.

fixtures.reasoning: H 216, a genuine cool BLUE, distinct from the cyan of the floor track at H 190-198 by 20 degrees at similar saturation. This is materials.ACCENTS['cool_blue'] territory and it belongs at the perimeter and high up. Three cool registers plus one warm key in a single room -- these interiors are not two-tone.

fixtures.placement: large backlit chequerboard panel in the wall, full height of the upper level; two attested, one magenta and one near-neutral

Hue constant at H 299-302 across a 1.7x value range with R = B to three decimals at every level -- a real MAGENTA, not a cast. Normalised (1.000, 0.826, 1.000) sRGB, linear (1.000, 0.649, 1.000). The NEUTRAL VARIANT is equally attested in the same frame at (0.945,0.05)-(0.995,0.40): (0.770,0.717,0.757) S 0.069, normalised (1.000, 0.931, 0.983), ~6250 K.

fixtures.placement: concealed high-level house lighting, fitting never in frame; a broad soft near-neutral wash over the whole chamber
fixtures.source: reference/05-sector-green/council chambers.webp (authority 1), gains recomputed as 0.9975/1.0820/0.9318, reproducing GREY_WORLD_GAINS. THE COLOUR IS THE FRAME'S OWN NEUTRALITY: the chamber's brightest surface, the perforated table fascia at (0.40,0.640)-(0.61,0.730), balances to 0.649/0.653/0.639, S 0.021 -- neutral to within 2%. Floor 0.426/0.488/0.493 (Y 0.475) at the region materials.py already cites, 0.434/0.433/0.376 (Y 0.429) below the fascia. THE EVENNESS IS THE MEASUREMENT: p50/p95 of the balanced frame excluding clipped sources is 0.397, against 0.06-0.24 for every other space in the family, and only 8.4% of the frame sits below Y 0.05 against 35-56% in the Zocalo, Fresh Air and the Dugout.
fixtures.extrapolated: Everything about the fitting -- kind, height, range -- because no fitting is visible. What is measured is the RESULT: a soft neutral wash at a fill ratio of 0.21, and that is what the engine has to reproduce however it is rigged.
fixtures.reasoning: The family's one counter-example, and it is a counter-example for a reason: the ceremonial room is lit like a room, the commercial rooms are lit like sets of pools. Its fill is 0.21 against 0.04-0.10 everywhere else and its brightest surface is NEUTRAL where every other space in the family is warm. That contrast is Green sector's identity and it should not be flattened by a single station-wide lighting rig.

fixtures.placement: backlit fine-perforated screen forming the whole front fascia of the council table, roughly 0.15-1.0 m above the floor, ~6 m run
fixtures.source: reference/05-sector-green/council chambers.webp. Balanced over (0.40,0.640)-(0.61,0.730): 0.649/0.653/0.639, H 77 S 0.021, V 0.653, Y 0.652 -- the brightest surface in the frame and essentially neutral. Raw it is (0.651,0.604,0.686) H 274 S 0.120, i.e. the frame's own magenta cast; k-means gives four bands at H 268-313 with saturation 0.085-0.125, so the RAW hue is capture, not fitting. Magnified at 3x it resolves as a fine square perforation grid with warm-tan dots on a pale ground. The floor below it reads Y 0.429 and the table top above it Y 0.338, so the fascia is 1.5x the floor and 1.9x the table.
fixtures.extrapolated: energy_rel 0.4 and range 3.0 m. The fascia is a low, wide, dim source and nothing in the frame separates its contribution from the house wash.
fixtures.reasoning: A low-level, wide, NEUTRAL emissive band -- the same compositional move as the conference lounge's cyan floor track and the Zocalo's deck strip, but neutral instead of coloured, which is again the ceremonial room refusing the accent every other space takes.

fixtures.placement: inside a shallow cone shade hung below standing eye height, one per table, as hospitality.py records and asserts
fixtures.source: reference/04-sector-red/Doug's Dugout.webp, RAW ONLY. materials.NEGATIVE_RESULTS forbids this frame for albedo and its gains recompute to (0.7235, 1.2793, 1.1961), reproducing that entry exactly -- but an emitter's colour is the illuminant rather than a reflectance, so the frame is usable for exactly this. The near pendant's rim at (0.400,0.062)-(0.650,0.094) is FULLY CLIPPED (median 1.000/0.965/1.000, S 0.035) so it gives intensity, not colour. The colour comes from the brightest resolved lit object inside its pool, the bun at (0.535,0.780)-(0.590,0.830): raw (0.867, 0.663, 0.569), H 19 S 0.344, normalised (1.000, 0.765, 0.656) sRGB, linear (1.000, 0.554, 0.393), ~3900 K. FILL: the table under the pendant reads Y 0.113 while the wall between pendants at (0.055,0.60)-(0.115,0.80) reads Y 0.008 and at (0.855,0.62)-(0.905,0.86) Y 0.013, and the ceiling between them Y 0.058. Fill/key 0.07-0.11.
fixtures.extrapolated: The colour rests on the bun's albedo being pale and warm-neutral, which it is not exactly -- it is bread. The deep H 0-8 readings elsewhere in that frame (the table at (1.000, 0.391, 0.305), the shade's underside at (1.000, 0.513, 0.484)) are the objects' own colour plus falloff, not the lamp, and taking them literally would put the pendant at 1500-1800 K, which nothing else in the family supports. spacing_m 2.2 is hospitality.py's table pitch, reproduced not measured.
fixtures.reasoning: materials.bar_pendant_lamp currently carries ACCENTS['warm_practical'] at 2440 K and energy 9.0. The energy is right -- this fitting is the sole source in its room and its rim clips completely white while 56.2% of the frame sits below Y 0.05, the most extreme distribution in the family. The colour is too saturated by the same margin as light_downlight's. Shadows: the pendant IS the design, so the two or three nearest ones cast and the rest do not.

fixtures.placement: wall-mounted neon figure on the left wall at roughly 1.8-2.6 m, plus a vertical cyan tube in four segments split by three clamp bands (hospitality.py)
fixtures.extrapolated: energy_rel and range, judged from its glow on the wall around it in a room with no ambient at all.
fixtures.reasoning: The Dugout's only cool light, against nine warm pendants. Even the darkest, warmest room in the family carries a cool accent.

fixtures.placement: backlit brand panel on the rear wall at roughly 1.6-2.2 m

Normalised on the median, (0.274, 0.517, 1.000) sRGB, linear (0.061, 0.230, 1.000). A SECOND signage source in the same frame is a red LED dot-matrix panel at (0.225,0.035)-(0.340,0.265): median (0.259, 0.086, 0.094) H 357 S 0.667, normalised (1.000, 0.332, 0.363), linear (1.000, 0.090, 0.108).

fixtures.reasoning: Two more signage emitters, blue and red, in a room whose architectural lighting is nine identical pendants. In a space with fill at 0.07-0.11 the signage is a real fraction of what the eye actually receives, and dropping it leaves the background of every Dugout shot black.

fixtures.placement: continuous glazed band around the saucer, ~2.4 m tall, divided into bays by solid piers; lit interior visible through it
fixtures.source: reference/04-sector-red/Earhart's.webp (authority 1). NEW GAINS, computed here: (0.8525, 0.9901, 1.2240), n=279,426. Measured RAW because what is being read is emission through glazing. K-means over the centre bay (0.435,0.385)-(0.605,0.535): (0.559,0.619,0.710) H 216 S 0.212 / (0.415,0.451,0.578) H 227 / (0.313,0.315,0.425) H 239 / (0.216,0.198,0.281) H 253 / (0.118,0.102,0.167) H 254 / (0.035,0.029,0.044) H 265. Hue constant H 216-265 across a TWENTY-FOLD range of value -- the cleanest tint measurement in the family. Normalised on the brightest cluster, (0.787, 0.872, 1.000) sRGB, linear (0.582, 0.733, 1.000), ~10000 K. LEVEL: that cluster is Y 0.613 against the daylit exterior shell above it at (0.05,0.10)-(0.60,0.26), balanced Y 0.340, i.e. the lit band reads 1.75x the surface beside it; the dark interior voids between bays read Y 0.031, i.e. 0.09x.
fixtures.extrapolated: energy_rel is 1.0 by definition (it is the only fitting in this frame). range_m 8.0 is the glazing's own depth into the room, judged from the visible interior, not measured.
fixtures.reasoning: This is the datum the standing blocking finding against exterior_approach needs: a lit interior seen from outside is NOT a uniform glow. It is a 1.75x/0.09x checker -- bright bays against dark ones, at a cool 10000 K -- and it is the DARK bays that make it read as a building rather than a lightbox. Also worth noting for its own sake: the interior register visible here is cool blue, while the concourse two decks below is warm-over-cool. The restaurants are cooler than the market.

ambient.source: reference/04-sector-red/more zocalo.png, balanced 0.936/1.137/0.951. Darkest MEASURABLE structural surface: the soffit above the gallery fascia at (0.60,0.005)-(0.75,0.022), Y 0.062, and the purlin run at (0.640,0.040)-(0.760,0.080), Y 0.062 (the gallery slab edge at Y 0.028 is nearly crushed and is not used). Brightest lit surface: the clean deck field at (0.215,0.815)-(0.315,0.859), Y 0.657. 0.062/0.657 = 0.094. Cross-check in reference/04-sector-red/zocalo.webp (gains 0.906/1.185/0.950): the side wall at (0.855,0.110)-(0.900,0.290) reads Y 0.464 and the same wall out of the fittings' reach at (0.900,0.330)-(0.980,0.430) reads Y 0.0685 -- 0.148. Whole-frame p50/p95 excluding clipped sources: 0.138 (more zocalo), 0.241 (zocalo, where a close crowd dominates the mid-tones). SEPARATE AND DO NOT CONFUSE: a chair leg on the deck casts a shadow only 0.74 as dark as the deck beside it, because ~4 downlight pools overlap at any point (spacing/height 2.7/7.2 = 0.375) and one occluder removes only one of them.

reference/04-sector-red/Casino.webp, balanced 1.014/1.071/0.926 (recomputed 1.0145/1.0707/0.9257). THE BEST-DEFINED RATIO IN THE FAMILY because it is one surface, one material, one depth: the deck at (0.28,0.90)-(0.40,1.00) carries hard grille shadow stripes thrown from the upper-left backlit panel. Balanced, p97 of that patch is 0.583 and p05 is 0.043 -- 0.074. The p90/p10 pair over the same patch is 0.515/0.087 = 0.168, which is the shallower figure for a shadow immediately adjacent to a lit stripe and therefore receiving bounce from it.
